ages.label: The Divine Ages
ages.summary: From the first powers to the settled rule of Zeus.

ages.label: The Heroic Generations
ages.summary: The deeds of the generations before Troy, roughly from the oldest to the youngest.

ages.label: The Trojan War
ages.summary: The war as the Epic Cycle told it, poem by poem.

ages.label: Outside Time
ages.summary: The standing order of gods and world: things that always are, rather than things that happened once.

periods.label: Primordial
periods.summary: The first powers: Chaos, Earth, Sky and Night; Oceanus and Tethys, whom Homer calls the origin of the gods.

periods.label: Titanomachy
periods.summary: The reign and fall of Cronus; the war of the Olympians against the Titans; Zeus, Poseidon and Hades divide the world by lot.

periods.label: Theomachy
periods.summary: Strife inside the new Olympian order: the plot to bind Zeus, Hephaestus hurled from heaven, Hera hung from the sky.

periods.label: Gigantomachy
periods.summary: Challengers to Zeus: the Giants, Typhon, and the Aloadae who piled Ossa on Olympus.

periods.label: The First Kings
periods.summary: The founders of the oldest royal houses: Erechtheus of Athens, born of the earth and raised by Athena, and Dardanus, son of Zeus, founder of the line of Troy.

periods.label: Perseus
periods.summary: Danae, the Gorgon, and Andromeda: the earliest great hero of Argos.

periods.label: Pelops and His Sons
periods.summary: Pelops, driver of horses, and his sons Atreus and Thyestes, through whose hands the scepter made by Hephaestus came down to Agamemnon.

periods.label: Bellerophon
periods.summary: The hero of Corinth and Lycia who killed the Chimaera.

periods.label: Heracles
periods.summary: His birth and labors, the first sack of Troy, and the war on Pylos.

periods.label: Jason & the Argonauts
periods.summary: The voyage of the Argo for the Golden Fleece.

periods.label: Theseus & Crete
periods.summary: Minos, the Minotaur, Ariadne, and the hero of Athens.

periods.label: Lapiths & Centaurs
periods.summary: The Lapiths of Thessaly against the wild Centaurs, in the days of Nestor’s youth.

periods.label: The Calydonian Boar
periods.summary: Meleager, the boar sent by Artemis, and the war of the Curetes and Aetolians.

periods.label: The Theban Wars
periods.summary: Oedipus, the Seven against Thebes, and the Epigoni.

periods.label: Nestor’s Youth
periods.summary: The wars of Pylos: Nestor’s cattle raid, the Epeians, Ereuthalion.

periods.label: Before Troy
periods.summary: The generation of the war is born and raised: Peleus weds Thetis, Achilles grows up in Phthia, the earlier kings of Troy.

periods.label: Cypria
periods.summary: The Plan of Zeus, the Judgment of Paris, Helen’s abduction, the gathering at Aulis, and nine years of war and raiding.

periods.label: Iliad
periods.summary: The wrath of Achilles, in the tenth year of the war.

periods.label: Aethiopis
periods.summary: Penthesilea and Memnon come to Troy’s aid; the death of Achilles.

periods.label: Little Iliad
periods.summary: The Judgment of Arms, the madness of Ajax, Philoctetes, Neoptolemus, and the Wooden Horse.

periods.label: Iliupersis
periods.summary: The sack of Troy.

periods.label: Nostoi
periods.summary: The returns of the Achaeans: storms, shipwrecks, and Agamemnon’s murder.

periods.label: Odyssey
periods.summary: The wanderings and homecoming of Odysseus.

periods.label: Telegony
periods.summary: Odysseus’ last journeys and his death at the hands of Telegonus, his son by Circe.

periods.label: The Divine Order
periods.summary: How the gods live and how the world is arranged: Olympus, Oceanus, the Ethiopians, the gods’ houses and feasts.

modes.label: Narrated
modes.summary: Told by the poet as part of the action.

modes.label: Told by a character
modes.summary: A character tells the story at length.

modes.label: Allusion
modes.summary: Mentioned in passing; the audience is expected to know the rest.

modes.label: Foreshadowing
modes.summary: A future event predicted, prayed for, or feared.

modes.label: Backstory
modes.summary: Earlier events that explain the present situation.
